title: Final: generics
cards/0/task: The method creates a T and compares values. It must work with int, and must reject string.
cards/1/q: where T : struct, new() — what does the compiler say?
cards/1/options/0: Error: a struct always has a parameterless constructor, so new() is not allowed with it
cards/1/explain: With struct, new T() is already allowed.
cards/2/q: You pass an IEnumerable<Cat> where an IEnumerable<Animal> is expected. Does it work?
cards/2/explain: Covariance works for reference types in interfaces and delegates.
cards/3/options/1: For reference-type T the JIT emits shared code
cards/3/options/2: object[] arr = new string[1]; arr[0] = 1; fails at run time
cards/3/explain: string is a reference type, so it is not unmanaged.
cards/4/q: Match the task to the constraint
cards/5/explain: An unconstrained T cannot be null — T might be int. default always works.
cards/6/q: The constraint that allows T x = null
cards/6/explain: Only reference types (and Nullable<T>) can be null.
cards/7/q: Why did C# 11 add static abstract interface members?
cards/7/options/0: So a generic can require operators and static properties — like + and Zero on numbers
cards/7/explain: INumber<T> and all of generic math are built on this.
